correctness.rationale: For an ordinary positive Bernoulli-thinned law of maximum count n, its parent has maximum count at most n, and the inverse pgf is unique. The (n−1) coefficient is n τ^(−n)(τ EW^(n−1)−EW^n) and is negative for τ below (a+n−1)/(a+b+n−1). At this boundary, a finite hypergeometric ODE gives an exact descending recurrence from q_n>0 and q_(n−1)=0, with positive denominators and a positive q_(j+2) coefficient, proving q_j>0 for all j≤n−2 and normalization Q(1)=1. The one-trial case and fixed-retention nesting are explicit. The general proof is analytic; 162 independent exact rational checks replay reconstruction and strict lower-bound obstruction.

originality.rationale: Theorem 19 of Kella–Löpker gives a general polynomial root maximum for binomial mixtures, not a closed-form root selection or recurrence for all beta-shape parameters. Their Example 10 explicitly evaluates only the uniform Beta(1,1) mixture and its parent hole. The present result identifies the highest root for every Beta(a,b), a,b>0, and a positive constructive boundary parent, including all-shape top-atom asymptotics. Related quasi-Pólya and convolution-thinning papers use different kernels; exact-phrase, alias, parameter, inverse, dilation, and root-index searches did not locate the same explicit general-beta theorem. A possible older terminological equivalent remains a stated risk.

value.rationale: The beta-binomial is the standard finite-exchangeable/overdispersed Bernoulli count family, so its minimal ordinary-thinning parameter is a natural measure of how far it can be de-thinned. The result classifies the index exactly for every real beta shape and every n, strengthening the source’s one-parameter uniform-mixing case. The strict universal penultimate-root dominance, explicit positive parent recursion, unique hole, and asymptotic top mass are mathematically structural and reusable, not routine numeric substitutions or an arbitrary unmotivated slice.
